rows.english: Someone else might come and make yet another claim: Let's talk about that quotation above, where it said: Insofar as [these different beings] have differing perceptions Of a single thing, we say it has no reality. The idea being expressed here is that a single object can be appearing in three different ways. This is incorrect because, according to you, what's happening is that three different objects are appearing in three different ways. And this certainly is your position; remember, you were describing a situation where three different kinds of beings sit down together and look at a glass full of something that's wet and flowing. You said that there were three different objects, each confirmed by a valid perception, and that they were appearing in three different ways.

rows.english: Again consider this same situation. Even though it is not necessarily true that the valid perceptions are identical, it is possible for there to be three valid perceptions here which happen to be identical. This is because, as we have already established logically, there can be a case where by the force of karma three different objects, each one confirmed by a valid perception, start to exist. And since this is possible, then it is equally possible that, by the force of karma, three equivalent valid perceptions of a vessel could start to exist as well.

rows.acip: ,SEMS TZAM RANG RGYUD PA RNAMS KYIS, ,CHOS RNAMS NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB, ,RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB DANG, ,RANG BZHIN GYIS NI GRUB PA DANG, ,RDZAS SU GRUB PA'I RNAM GZHAG RNAMS, ,TSAD GRUB TU NI MDZAD PAR SNANG,
rows.wylie: sems tsam rang rgyud pa rnams kyis, ,chos rnams ngo bo nyid kyis grub, ,rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub dang, ,rang bzhin gyis ni grub pa dang, ,rdzas su grub pa'i rnam gzhag rnams, ,tshad grub tu ni mdzad par snang
rows.english: It would appear That those of the Mind-Only School And the Independent Group Hold presentations which say That the ideas that things Exist in and of themselves, Or exist by definition, Or exist through some nature of their own, Or exist substantially Are actually correct. The Mind-Only group is a step above both the Detailist and Sutrist schools, whom we've already heard from.  Their defining belief is that—when we are looking at a patch of blue—the blue which we see is not standing in the outside world; rather, we are watching a seed within our mind flower into a blue color which is also in our mind.  All of this seeing of the outside world is happening within a region of our own mind known as “storehouse consciousness.” The fourth and highest of the four schools of classical Buddhism is known as the “Middle Way.”  It is divided into two sections: the Independent Group, and the Consequence Group.  Members of the Independent Group believe that words, and logic, have an inborn capacity to express or prove things; which is to say, accurate words and correct logic should be perceived the same by any sane person. This then is what it means to say that these thinkers believe that some things could exist by definition, and so on—all the terms listed here refer to the same things.  Still though these opinions fail to allow for a world which is in every detail created by the seeds within our mind.
